solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Globe-trotting pleasure-seeker's black dog

parts.note: jet black; jet is a black stone
a setter is a gun dog

explanation.surface: Someone's black dog seems to be doing a lot of travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ’s is the link: the pleasure-seeker is black plus dog. The long hyphenated definition up front hides the short wordplay behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the jet set were the rich who flew between fashionable resorts in search of fun.

clue.text: A power held by fellow in charge of a flowering shrub

parts.note: Jon, a man's name
used as is
P for power, as in physics
i/c, in charge
used as is

explanation.surface: A strong man in charge of an ornamental bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellow is just a man's name here, an unusually loose way to clue one.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the usual British garden name for the flowering quince, a red-blossomed shrub.

clue.text: In Princeton, a likely description of much traditional music

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A remark about the music heard at Princeton University.
explanation.walkthrough: A likely reads as the start of the definition, but it is the end of the hiding place, which lets the clue flow as one sentence about music.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: most traditional Western music is written in a key, which is what tonal means.

clue.text: Impedes new copper prodding remains of fire

indicators.note: to prod is to poke into, so the letters go inside

parts.note: what is left glowing after a fire
N for new
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A rookie policeman poking the dying fire gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to encumber is to hamper or weigh down.

clue.text: Book about setting up of broadcast item, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means turned upward, reversed
the book goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a tome is a large book
SOW, to broadcast seed, set upward

explanation.surface: A book about how a broadcast programme was put together.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast is the farming sense, scattering seed. An item is a couple in a relationship, and possibly marks that as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a couple who are an item form one kind of twosome.

clue.text: Copy beginning of record I found in unexpected place

indicators.note: I is placed among the letters
the letters of place are rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of record
I goes in among the letters of PLACE, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A copy of a record turns up somewhere it should not be.
explanation.walkthrough: Unexpected place reads as a location, but unexpected is telling you to rearrange place.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a replica is an exact copy of an original.

clue.text: Notes written about island capital

indicators.note: the notes are written around the island, holding it inside

parts.note: SO and FA, two notes of the sol-fa scale
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A remark about someone writing notes on an island's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: Island capital reads as one phrase, but the island is wordplay and only capital defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Bulgaria's capital is one of many capitals.

clue.text: Tantrum left parents finally upset

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of parents is used
in a down clue, set up means turned upside down

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
last letter of parents

explanation.surface: A child throws a tantrum and the parents end up upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Left looks like the verb, but it is the nautical side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to be in a strop is to be in a bad-tempered sulk.

clue.text: Healthy old actor catching game for supplier of healthy food

indicators.note: the first word catches the game inside it

parts.note: fit means healthy
RU is rugby union
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A fit veteran actor playing a sport tells us where to find health food.
explanation.walkthrough: Old actor in crosswords is very often the Victorian theatre manager, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a tree bearing fruit supplies food that is good for you.

clue.text: States 18 opposed

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
18 down is ENGLISH, abbreviated E

explanation.walkthrough: The number points at the answer to 18 down, and its usual abbreviation is what is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be averse to something is to be opposed to it.

clue.text: Grass — giving rise to great alarm!

definitions.meaning: a genus of grasses related to millet, Panicum

explanation.surface: An informer's betrayal causing a scare, with grass as British slang for informer.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass invites the British slang sense of informing on someone, as in grassing up a friend; here it is simply the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a botanist's name for a millet-like grass genus, and the everyday word for sudden fright.

clue.text: Convenient haven in old Indian city

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the haven is placed in the city, inside its letters

parts.note: Pune, formerly Poona, a city near Mumbai
a port is a haven for ships

explanation.surface: A handy harbour found in an ancient city of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Indian city tempts you to look for a historic place name, but old is just O, placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something opportune comes at a convenient, well-chosen moment.

clue.text: Tyneside boss fencing in large aquatic plant

indicators.note: a fence surrounds what it encloses

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
the raised boss at the centre of a shield, from Latin
L for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A manager from Newcastle surrounding a big water plant, perhaps in a garden pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss here is not a manager but the knob on a shield. The fence is the two pieces together, with L landing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the lotus genus, whose big leaves and flowers rise above ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Hanger-on heading off with American force

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, comes off

parts.note: LIMPET, a proverbial hanger-on, minus its first letter L
US for American

explanation.surface: A clinging follower leaves, joined by American might.
explanation.walkthrough: A limpet clings to rocks, so a person who clings is called one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: impetus is the driving force or momentum behind something.

clue.text: Plant found in ravines by seabird with style

parts.note: a chine is a deep ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset
élan is flair or style
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A plant spotted growing in gorges near a bird with some panache.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two pieces do not come in clue order: bird with style means the bird has style alongside, and the style goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Physalis, a plant whose papery orange husks look like paper lanterns.

clue.text: Speech made by new president during month on river?

parts.note: in means during, as in in August
Aug is the calendar abbreviation
the Ural, a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A new president gives a speech in August by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is odd: presidents are sworn in in January, not August.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun use, chiefly American: short for inaugural address, given when a president takes office.

clue.text: Corrupt squire out to get semiprecious stone

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled out of their proper order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A dishonest country gentleman is thrown out and loses a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrupt squire reads as a crooked landowner, but corrupt is telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the blue-green mineral is one of the best-known semiprecious stones.

clue.text: Censure maiden cutting beautiful youth on horse

indicators.note: the maiden cuts into the youth

parts.note: Adonis, the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
H and horse are both slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A girl on horseback interrupts a handsome young man with a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden suggests a girl, but it is cricket: a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to admonish someone is to rebuke them, which is to censure.

clue.text: Boxer possibly mends tan briefs badly

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: A boxer doing a poor job of repairing his beige underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Boxer a fighter in need of new shorts; it is the dog breed, and possibly signals that a boxer is only one example of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a boxer is one breed of dog, and the dog is proverbially man's best friend.

clue.text: Language no good in priest's hole, initially?

indicators.note: no good is placed in the priest's name, inside its letters

parts.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
NG is the abbreviation for no good

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of hole is used

parts.note: first letter of hole

explanation.surface: A language with no use in a priest hole, a hiding place for Catholic priests in Tudor houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Priest's hole looks like one phrase, a secret chamber for hiding Catholic priests; the words split, and the priest is the biblical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the world's languages, and the one this crossword is written in.

clue.text: Insecure title oddly held by right-winger

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters

parts.note: a member of the British Conservative Party

indicators.note: those letters are held inside the right-winger

parts.note: letters 1, 3 and 5 of title

explanation.surface: A title is shakily held by a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly looks like an adverb for held, but it picks the odd letters of title.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the physical sense: something tottery is unsteady and liable to fall.

clue.text: Eccentric son at university going over grounds

parts.note: a cam is an eccentric, an off-centre disc on a rotating shaft

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means turning back up the column

parts.note: S for son
in British usage you are up at university while studying there

explanation.surface: An odd son is away at university, crossing the lawns.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccentric looks like an adjective for the son, but it is the engineering noun: an off-centre disc that turns rotation into back-and-forth motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrower sense: a campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Gawky being ultimately cut out for relaxing sport?

indicators.note: take the ultimate, last, letter

parts.note: gangling means tall and awkward

indicators.note: that letter is cut out of the word

parts.note: last letter of being, removed from the front

explanation.surface: An awkward person feels unsuited to a restful pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Being is not a creature here; only its last letter matters. The question mark flags that not every angler finds fishing relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: fishing with rod and line is often thought of as a calm, restful pursuit.

clue.text: Man absorbing woman's artistic style

indicators.note: the island takes the woman inside it

parts.note: IOM, the Isle of Man
Di, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man takes on the look of a woman's art.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is not a person but the island in the Irish Sea. The ’s is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: in the arts an idiom is a characteristic mode of expression, as in the classical idiom.

clue.text: Excursion a firm provides for colourful bird

parts.note: a tour is an excursion
used as is
CO, company, is a firm

explanation.surface: A travel company laying on a trip to see an exotic bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Provides for joins wordplay to definition: the pieces supply the bird. The word is also spelt turaco.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an African bird noted for its brilliant green and crimson plumage.

clue.text: Taxi turns up in main road? They can be counted on

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upward
the result goes inside the road

parts.note: the A1, main road from London to Edinburgh, written AI
CAB set upward

explanation.surface: A taxi appears on the main road; drivers who can be relied upon.
explanation.walkthrough: They can be counted on sounds like reliable people, but these are literally counted on, beads and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: abaci are counting frames, so people do their counting on them.

clue.text: Murderer a Trojan prince observed, according to report

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so we go by the sound

parts.note: Paris, prince of Troy, plus eyed, meaning observed

explanation.surface: A killer was seen by a prince of Troy, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen. The a belongs with the prince, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrower sense than the definition: a parricide is someone who kills a parent or close relative.

clue.text: Arab, one fronting endless attack without question

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped
one stands at the front of what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the shortened attack goes round the question

parts.note: RAID with its last letter removed
Q for question

explanation.surface: An Arab leads a relentless assault without asking anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, not lacking, an old sense still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: people from Iraq are one of many Arab nationalities.

clue.text: State capital's second month without alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the two letters sit outside the drink

parts.note: S for second
M for month
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A capital city's alcohol-free second month, like a dry February.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ’s links definition and wordplay. Second month suggests February, but second and month are two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Oregon's capital, one of the fifty US state capitals.

clue.text: Like a tomboy's call to attract man by hotel

parts.note: hoy! is a shout to catch someone's attention
Denis, a man's name
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tomboy's attempt to get a man's attention outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ’s is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hoyden is a boisterous, rowdy girl, so hoydenish behaviour is tomboyish.
